chunks.subject: AP Microeconomics
chunks.title: Q3 Short FRQ (5 points) — Set 1: game theory (Bitaly's Bracelets)
chunks.content: AP Microeconomics FRQ 3 (Short), 5 points, one per element, based on a payoff matrix. Set 1 answer key highlights: state that Bitaly's Bracelets does not have a dominant strategy and explain that its best response depends on the rival's choice; identify the TWO Nash equilibria for the game; state the minimum amount (e.g., $6) required for a given outcome; plus related state/explain elements. Common failure: asserting a dominant strategy where none exists; identifying only one Nash equilibrium; reading the payoff matrix from the wrong player's perspective.

chunks.subject: AP Microeconomics
chunks.title: Q3 Set 1 exemplar — Sample 3A, 5/5
chunks.content: Q3 (Set 1) scored 5/5 — stated no dominant strategy with a best-response explanation, identified both Nash equilibria, and gave the correct minimum amount. Full-credit model for the game-theory FRQ.

chunks.subject: AP Microeconomics
chunks.title: Q3 Set 1 exemplar — Sample 3B, 4/5
chunks.content: Q3 (Set 1) scored 4/5 — earned most elements but lost one, commonly the explanation of why there is no dominant strategy or one of the two Nash equilibria. Illustrates a strong response one point short.

chunks.subject: AP Microeconomics
chunks.title: Q3 Set 1 exemplar — Sample 3C, 1/5
chunks.content: Q3 (Set 1) scored 1/5 — earned only one element, losing the dominant-strategy explanation, the two Nash equilibria, and the minimum-amount answer. Illustrates a response that misreads the payoff matrix or the game concepts.
